title: A Survey on Human Interaction Motion Generation
summary: Organizes human-human, human-object and human-scene generation with datasets and evaluation; useful for backward citation chasing across interaction types.
limitations: A survey taxonomy is a discovery aid; individual method capabilities still require checking the cited primary papers.

title: Motion Generation: A Survey of Generative Approaches and Benchmarks
summary: Reviews generative model families, conditioning, datasets and metrics, emphasizing recent motion-generation literature.
limitations: Architecture-based grouping does not by itself distinguish semantic composition from sequence concatenation.

title: Text-driven Motion Generation: Overview, Challenges and Directions
summary: Reviews text-to-motion through architecture and discrete/continuous representation perspectives.
limitations: Text-to-motion quality is not automatically evidence of unseen skill-pair or interaction-state generalization.

title: Human Motion Video Generation: A Survey
summary: Adjacent literature: surveys human-motion video generation, including planning, generation and refinement across visual, text and audio conditions.
limitations: Video appearance and motion plausibility do not establish valid 3D contact or executable motion; keep outside 3D-motion numerical rankings.

title: CFGComposer: Compositional Audio-Text-to-Motion Generation via Copula Score Correction
summary: Composes audio and text motion diffusion scores while learning a cross-modal correction for their dependence; relevant to model-level composition beyond text-only actions.
limitations: The correction is jointly trained: this should not be described as entirely training-free combination of independent priors. Reported deployment and benchmarks have not been independently reproduced here.

title: EDGE: Editable Dance Generation From Music
summary: Music-conditioned diffusion supports joint-wise constraints and temporal in-betweening, connecting body-part control with long dance editing.
limitations: Music-conditioned dance editing is adjacent to skill composition; its physical-plausibility metric is not full interaction-dynamics certification.

title: Lodge: A Coarse to Fine Diffusion Network for Long Dance Generation Guided by the Characteristic Dance Primitives
summary: Global diffusion generates characteristic dance primitives; parallel local diffusion expands them into detailed long sequences, with a foot refinement component.
limitations: Coarse-to-fine music choreography does not test object-state dependencies or task-completion composition.

title: EMAGE: Towards Unified Holistic Co-Speech Gesture Generation via Expressive Masked Audio Gesture Modeling
summary: Audio and masked gesture hints drive holistic face/body/hand/global motion with compositional quantized priors; introduces BEAT2.
limitations: A compositional representation across body streams is distinct from unseen semantic task-chain generalization.

title: FineDance: A Fine-grained Choreography Dataset for 3D Full Body Dance Generation
summary: Full-body music-dance dataset with detailed hand motion and dance genres; its retrieval and generation mechanisms provide an adjacent composition setting.
limitations: Dance genre and beat metrics do not substitute for action order, contact and object-state correctness.

title: MoMask: Generative Masked Modeling of 3D Human Motions
summary: Hierarchical residual quantization and masked token generation provide a discrete motion prior with text-guided temporal inpainting.
limitations: A useful backbone or inpainting capability does not by itself prove composition of independent skills or object-aware tasks.

title: RealisMotion: Decomposed Human Motion Control and Video Generation in the World Space
summary: Separates subject, background, world-space trajectory and action controls for human video composition.
limitations: Adjacent video-generation evidence; does not imply a joint human-object 3D generator or physically executable controller.

title: Multi-Modal Controlled Coherent Motion Generation
summary: Combines text, speech and trajectory denoisers by body region and recurrently assembles a holistic motion at each diffusion step.
method: Four modality/component denoisers use body masks; a timeline can reassign parts and an LLM can plan intervals.
conditions: Concurrent speech audio, action text and target trajectory; no paired multimodal training set required by the author description.
evaluation: Author page: 1,000 concurrent-control clips built from 40 text descriptions and 694 speech clips; evaluates text and speech fidelity.
limitations: Default part assignment can conflict when text and speech both request upper-body actions. Controlled consistency benchmark does not establish arbitrary cross-modal semantic generalization.
evidence_locator: Author page: Spatially decoupled denoising; Benchmark; Limitations. Project-page audit, not full-paper replication.

title: Template Free Reconstruction of Human-object Interaction with Procedural Interaction Generation
summary: Procedurally creates varied human-object interaction pairs and trains an image-conditioned reconstruction model for unseen objects.
limitations: Interaction-pair synthesis and reconstruction are distinct from continuous motion composition; static data counts must not be reported as motion hours.

title: FUSION: Full-Body Unified Motion Prior for Body and Hands via Diffusion
summary: Unifies body and hand datasets into a full-body motion prior, with optimization-driven object-motion and self-interaction applications.
limitations: The object-guided application consumes object motion; it is not evidence for text-plus-initial-state dynamic interaction generation.

title: InterMask: 3D Human Interaction Generation via Collaborative Masked Modelling
summary: Collaboratively predicts masked discrete motion tokens for two people and also supports reaction generation.
limitations: Two-person interaction and reaction generation do not by themselves establish arbitrary actor-count or object-state task composition.

title: ParaHome: Parameterizing Everyday Home Activities Towards 3D Generative Modeling of Human-Object Interactions
summary: Captures full-body, hand, multi-object and articulated-object activity in a home setting, including sequential and concurrent manipulations.
limitations: Real continuous task recordings are distinct from constructed skill combinations; capture/participant grouping and future-condition leakage need independent protocol checks.
